originalTitle: Nvidia says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
summary: Starting Nvidia's quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, new board chair Harvey Jones said that when former CEO Jensen Huang resigned, "the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Jones added, "We will not be addressing or taking questions on today's call regarding the circumstances of Jensen's resignation […]
content: Starting Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, new board chair Harvey Jones said that when former CEO Jensen Huang resigned, “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Jones added, “We will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation.” Huang had publicly floated the idea of returning earlier on Tuesday. In a statement posted to X, he wrote that he “did not live up to the standards expected of everyone” at the company, that he regretted his mistakes, and that he would cooperate with the Nvidia board’s investigation into his actions. He added that he’d be willing to return to the chief executive role if offered it, though a day earlier, the Nvidia board reportedly said it was not considering bringing him back. “NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company,” Huang wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” But since his November 12th resignation, Huang remains entangled in scandal. He’s reportedly had three affairs, two with subordinates at Nvidia, one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset suspected of facilitating illicit chip sales. (Huang has pushed against restrictions on Nvidia chip sales in China.) He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st, and an internal company investigation is ongoing. Tech industry heavyweights have still voiced their support for Huang, dubbing him “irreplaceable” and petitioning for his return. Some have cast doubt on the allegations that Alice Huang (no relation) was spying on behalf of China and painted the leaks about their relationship as a conspiracy against the former CEO. President Donald Trump, a close ally of Huang for much of the past year, has also backed him. On Monday, Trump said he “would not mind” Huang returning, adding that “I think he learned a big lesson — I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another.” Trump’s closeness with Huang could also complicate things for Nvidia, however. The company has ramped up its lobbying in Washington, D.C., spending $5 million in 2025 and $4.7 million so far in 2026. But as Democrats prepare to take Congress, they’re planning to investigate Trump’s dealings with Big Tech and other industries, alleging potential corruption. “The election wasn’t very positive for AI, and [the news around Huang’s resignation] is only going to complicate things, especially for the company in particular but for AI as a whole going forward,” Brendan Glavin, director of insights at OpenSecrets, told The Verge in an interview last week. Lior Prosor, managing partner at Deep33, a tech VC firm, said last week that he didn’t expect Huang’s resignation to pop the AI bubble, although Huang has had a significant hand in mobilizing funds for the AI infrastructure buildout in the U.S. Under Huang’s leadership in August, Nvidia entered into partnerships with six financial institutions for about $500 billion to fund such endeavors. “NVIDIA supplies roughly 75 percent of the AI compute hardware the industry consumes, and demand continues to dramatically outpace supply,” Deep33’s Prosor said in an interview with The Verge. “Neither its customers nor its competitors can easily replace the capabilities it provides, and the economic incentives driving the AI trade remain unchanged.” Even so, a potential market cooling has some worried, as Anthropic’s IPO, slated to potentially be the largest of all time, is set for Thursday. The chipmaker had agreed to buy $10 billion in Anthropic shares via private placement, on top of a $10 billion funding promise Nvidia had already made last year.
chineseTitle: 英伟达表示不打算恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官
chineseSummary: 在周二开始的英伟达季度财报电话会议上，新任董事会主席哈维·琼斯表示，当前首席执行官黄仁勋辞职时，“英伟达董事会一致接受了他的辞职，并且不打算恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官。”琼斯补充说：“我们不会在今天的电话会议上就詹森辞职的情况发表讲话或回答问题[...]
chineseContent: 在周二开始的英伟达季度财报电话会议上，新任董事会主席哈维·琼斯表示，当前首席执行官黄仁勋辞职时，“英伟达董事会一致接受了他的辞职，并且不打算恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官。”琼斯补充说：“我们不会在今天的电话会议上就詹森辞职的情况和正在进行的调查提出问题。”黄在周二早些时候公开提出了回国的想法。在发布给 X 的一份声明中，他写道，他“没有达到公司每个人的期望”，他对自己的错误感到遗憾，并且他将配合 Nvidia 董事会对其行为的调查。他补充说，如果有机会的话，他愿意重返首席执行官职位，但据报道，英伟达董事会在一天前表示，不考虑让他回归。 “NVIDIA 是一家百年一遇的公司，”黄仁勋写道。 “如果董事会认为我的回归符合我们的股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益，我将很荣幸回应这些呼吁并重新担任首席执行官。”但自11月12日辞职以来，黄仍然深陷丑闻之中。据报道，他有过三起婚外情，其中两起是与英伟达的下属发生关系，另一起是与一名涉嫌协助非法芯片销售的中国情报人员发生关系。 （黄先生反对对 Nvidia 芯片在中国销售的限制。）他计划于 12 月 1 日在国会作证，公司内部调查正在进行中。科技行业重量级人物仍然表达了对黄的支持，称他“不可替代”，并请愿他回归。一些人对黄爱丽（无亲属关系）代表中国进行间谍活动并画下警告的指控表示怀疑。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
